title: 2027 Chase Leadership Development Program – Summer Analyst Opportunity in the USA
summary: The 2027 Chase Leadership Development Program (CLDP) Summer Analyst Opportunity is now open for students interested in gaining hands-on experience in financial services, business strategy, product development, project management, analytics, and emerging technology. Offered by JPMorgan Chase Co. through its Consumer Community Banking division, the program provides selected students with a 9-week summer analyst experience designed to introduce them to the Chase Leadership Development Program and prepare high-performing candidates for potential full-time opportunities after graduation. The 2027 Summer Analyst Program is available in Columbus, Ohio; Wilmington, Delaware; and Plano, Texas , giving eligible students an opportunity to gain practical corporate experience while working on projects that have a real-world impact on customers and the business. The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM . However, applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the program may close earlier once available positions are filled. Students who meet the eligibility requirements are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible. What Is the Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst Opportunity? The Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst Opportunity is a summer internship experience within JPMorgan Chase s Consumer Community Banking business. The program is structured as a 9-week introduction to the full-time Chase Leadership Development Program . During the summer, analysts receive exposure to Chase s businesses and work on projects intended to provide measurable value to the organization and its customers. Rather than being limited to one narrow area of banking, the program provides exposure to a broad range of functions and business areas. These include: Auto Business Banking Card Services Connected Commerce Consumer Banking Digital Product Experience Finance Home Lending J.P. Morgan Wealth Management Marketing Controls Operations Risk Management Strategy and Strategic Initiatives Summer Analysts are placed into roles focused on one of three primary disciplines: Product Project/Program Management Strategy Strategic Initiatives This structure allows participants to develop a broader understanding of how a major financial institution develops products, manages complex projects, makes strategic decisions, evaluates risk, and serves customers. What Does a Chase Summer Analyst Do? The Summer Analyst role is designed to provide meaningful exposure to real business challenges rather than simply observational work. Participants may contribute to projects involving data, product development, strategy, marketing, operations, risk, technology, and cross-functional collaboration. Key responsibilities include: 1. Data Analytics and Business Decision-Making Summer Analysts may use data analytics to evaluate operational effectiveness and help support business decisions. This can involve: Measuring operational performance Analyzing business data Supporting risk-versus-reward decisions Assessing profitability Forecasting financial outcomes Identifying opportunities for improvement This component makes analytical ability particularly important for candidates interested in the program. 2. Product Development Participants may contribute to the development of financial products and services throughout their lifecycle. This can include: Testing new features Iterating products based on findings Measuring performance Evaluating customer response Supporting product marketing Helping develop new and emerging financial solutions Students interested in product management, technology, marketing, business development, or customer experience may find this particularly relevant. 3. Project and Program Management Analysts may also support project management efforts associated with high-visibility Chase brands and initiatives. This can include work related to: Marketing initiatives Media initiatives Business projects Cross-functional coordination Project planning Implementation Performance measurement The role therefore requires candidates who can organize information, manage priorities, collaborate with different teams, and help move projects forward. 4. Business Strategy and Regulatory Controls Summer Analysts may evaluate and quantify business strategies while taking regulatory controls into consideration. This provides exposure to the relationship between: Business strategy Financial performance Risk Regulation Operational controls Customer outcomes Students interested in strategy, finance, risk management, consulting, or financial services can gain valuable experience from this aspect of the program. 5. Cross-Functional Problem Solving The program emphasizes collaboration across different business functions. Depending on the assignment, analysts may work with teams such as: Engineering Brand Legal Compliance Finance UX Design Product Operations Strategy This provides participants with an opportunity to understand how large organizations bring together people with different technical and professional backgrounds to solve complex business problems. 6. AI-Enabled Solutions The 2027 program also highlights the use of artificial intelligence in business operations. Participants may have opportunities to: Design AI-enabled solutions Build and deploy solutions that automate workflows Improve decision-making Enhance customer and stakeholder experiences Evaluate AI models Monitor AI-enabled systems Apply responsible AI controls This makes the opportunity particularly relevant for students interested in the intersection of business, finance, analytics, technology, and artificial intelligence . Training and Professional Development One of the major features of the Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst experience is its emphasis on professional development. Participants have access to structured training designed to strengthen both business knowledge and professional skills. The program provides a support network that includes: A dedicated program manager Professional mentors Senior leaders Managers Peer mentors Participants can also receive frequent feedback and coaching throughout the internship. This environment is intended to help students understand their strengths, improve their professional capabilities, develop their personal brand, and build meaningful professional relationships. Potential Pathway to a Full-Time Career The Summer Analyst Program can serve as an entry point into the broader Chase Leadership Development Program . Successful completion of the summer program may result in an offer of employment into the CLDP full-time program , which is described as a two-year rotational program . This is an important feature for students who are looking beyond a short-term internship and are interested in developing a longer-term career at JPMorgan Chase. However, completion of the summer program does not mean that every participant is automatically guaranteed a full-time position. The opportunity states that successful completion may result in an offer. Required Skills and Qualifications Candidates should demonstrate a combination of analytical ability, communication skills, professionalism, curiosity, and problem-solving ability. The required capabilities include: Analytical Skills Applicants should have exceptional analytical skills and demonstrate strong technical learning ability. Candidates should be comfortable learning new concepts and using information to understand and solve business problems. Intellectual Curiosity The program looks for students who demonstrate: Curiosity Willingness to learn Interest in understanding how businesses work Motivation to explore new ideas Microsoft Office Skills Applicants should be proficient in: Microsoft Excel Microsoft Word Microsoft PowerPoint These tools are important for analysis, documentation, presentations, and communicating business recommendations. Communication Skills Strong interpersonal and communication skills are required. Candidates should be able to communicate effectively with colleagues, managers, and other stakeholders. Teamwork and Collaboration The program operates in a highly collaborative environment, so candidates should be comfortable working as part of a team. The position specifically emphasizes being: Proactive A team player Professional Collaborative Project Management and Problem Solving Candidates should demonstrate excellent: Project management skills Problem-solving skills Collaboration skills These abilities are particularly relevant because Summer Analysts may work on projects involving multiple teams and business functions. Adaptability Applicants should be able to thrive in a dynamic and changing environment. This is important because large financial institutions operate across multiple businesses, technologies, regulatory requirements, and customer needs. Interest in Financial Innovation Candidates should have an interest in supporting innovative financial products and services. Preferred Academic Qualifications The preferred academic profile is particularly important for students considering applying. Applicants are expected to be pursuing one of the following: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) Bachelor of Science (B.S.) Fifth-year Master of Arts (M.A.) Fifth-year Master of Science (M.S.) The expected graduation window is: December 2027 through June 2028. The opportunity also lists a: Minimum GPA of 3.2 out of 4.0. The academic fields listed as a plus include: Actuarial Science Economics Engineering Finance Mathematics Operations Research Statistics Analytics Information Systems Emerging Technology in Business The wording indicates that coursework in these areas is an advantage rather than stating that applicants must necessarily major in one of these fields. Where Is the 2027 Chase Summer Analyst Program Located? The program is offered in three U.S. locations: Columbus, Ohio Columbus is one of the locations where selected Summer Analysts can be placed. Wilmington, Delaware Wilmington is another available program location. Plano, Texas Plano, Texas is the third listed location. Applicants are required to provide a location preference as part of their application. U.S. Work Authorization Requirement An important eligibility condition is that applicants must be authorized to work in the United States . JPMorgan Chase explicitly states that it does not offer employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program . The company also states that it will not provide assistance or sign documentation supporting other forms of immigration sponsorship or benefits, including: Optional Practical Training (OPT) Curricular Practical Training (CPT) Therefore, international students who require sponsorship or related immigration assistance should carefully consider this requirement before applying. Who Can Apply for the 2027 Chase Summer Analyst Opportunity? The opportunity is primarily designed for university students who meet the academic, graduation, work authorization, and skills requirements. A strong candidate would generally be someone who: Is pursuing a B.A., B.S., fifth-year M.A., or M.S. degree Expects to graduate between December 2027 and June 2028 Has a minimum GPA of 3.2/4.0 Has strong analytical skills Is comfortable learning technical concepts Has strong communication and interpersonal skills Can work effectively in teams Has project management and problem-solving capabilities Is proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint Is interested in innovative financial products and services Is authorized to work in the United States Can work in one of the listed U.S. program locations Coursework in areas such as finance, economics, analytics, mathematics, statistics, engineering, information systems, and emerging technology can be an advantage. Application Process The application process includes several stages. Step 1: Submit the Application Applicants must submit a complete application, including: Resume Location preference Relevant application information JPMorgan Chase emphasizes that applicants should complete all relevant questions carefully because the application and resume are used by the recruiting team to initially assess candidates. Step 2: Complete the Video Interview Candidates who meet the minimum application criteria will receive an invitation to complete a video interview powered by HireVue . The video interview provides candidates with an opportunity to expand on their resume and demonstrate their experience, communication skills, and suitability for the program. The HireVue interview is required. An application will not proceed to further review until the required video interview step has been completed. Step 3: Complete the Interview Promptly Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete the HireVue video interview within three days of receiving the invitation . This is particularly important because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Step 4: Rolling Review and Position Availability Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The employer strongly encourages candidates to apply and complete all required application components as early as possible because the program may close when available positions are filled. Application Deadline Deadline: December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM. However, applicants should not wait until the final deadline. Because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and positions can close as they are filled, submitting an application early may be important. Why Consider the Chase Leadership Development Program? The program offers several features that can make it valuable for students seeking a career in financial services, technology, analytics, strategy, product management, or business leadership. 1. Real-World Business Experience Participants work on projects designed to have a real impact on Chase s business and customers. 2. Exposure to Multiple Business Areas The program provides exposure to numerous areas of a major financial services organization, from consumer banking and card services to digital products, finance, risk, operations, and strategy. 3. Professional Mentorship Participants receive support from program managers, mentors, senior leaders, managers, and peers. 4. Skills Development The program provides structured training intended to strengthen business acumen, professional capabilities, and technical skills. 5. Networking Participants can build relationships with colleagues, mentors, senior leaders, and other students participating in the program. 6. Potential Full-Time Opportunity Successful completion of the Summer Analyst Program may lead to an offer to join the two-year CLDP full-time rotational program. 7. Exposure to Emerging Technology The program includes work involving AI-enabled solutions, workflow automation, decision-making, customer experience, and responsible AI controls. Benefits and Employee Support JPMorgan Chase states that it offers a competitive total rewards package and a range of benefits for eligible employees. The broader benefits described by the organization include: Comprehensive healthcare coverage On-site health and wellness centers Retirement savings plans Backup childcare Tuition reimbursement Mental health support Financial coaching The specific compensation and benefits applicable to a particular position are provided during the hiring process and depend on eligibility. Diversity and Inclusion JPMorgan Chase states that it is committed to an inclusive work environment and values the diverse backgrounds, experiences, and skills of its workforce. The company describes itself as an equal opportunity employer and states that it does not discriminate based on protected characteristics, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy, disability, or other characteristics protected by applicable law. The company also states that reasonable accommodations are available for applicants and employees with disabilities and certain other needs. Click HERE to read more. How to Prepare a Strong Application Students interested in this opportunity should make sure their application clearly demonstrates how their background matches the program. 1. Tailor Your Resume Focus your resume on experiences demonstrating: Analytical ability Leadership Problem solving Project management Teamwork Communication Technology Business knowledge Data analysis 2. Highlight Measurable Achievements Where possible, demonstrate the impact of your work using measurable results. For example, instead of simply saying that you worked on a project, explain what you contributed and what outcome was achieved. 3. Demonstrate Your Interest in Financial Services The program is designed around financial products, services, customers, business strategy, and innovation. Candidates should be prepared to explain why they are interested in these areas. 4. Prepare for the HireVue Interview Because the video interview is a required part of the process, applicants should prepare examples demonstrating: Leadership Teamwork Problem solving Adaptability Communication Initiative Handling challenges Learning new skills 5. Apply Early Do not treat December 1, 2026, as the only date that matters. Since applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and positions may close once filled, early application is strongly recommended. APPLY HERE Conclusion The 2027 Chase Leadership Development Program Summer Analyst Opportunity provides university students with a structured nine-week introduction to one of JPMorgan Chase s leadership development pathways. Through exposure to product management, project management, strategy, analytics, financial services, technology, risk, marketing, and other business functions, participants can gain practical experience while developing their professional and technical capabilities. The program is particularly relevant for students interested in finance, business strategy, analytics, technology, product management, operations, and financial innovation . Participants can also benefit from mentorship, structured training, networking, coaching, and exposure to senior leaders. An additional advantage is the potential pathway from the summer experience into the two-year Chase Leadership Development Program , although such a full-time opportunity depends on successful completion and is not guaranteed. Students who meet the academic and work authorization requirements should pay close attention to the rolling application process. With the stated deadline of December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM , and positions potentially closing earlier as they are filled, submitting a complete application early is strongly recommended. title: Nordic Baltic Youth Summit 2026 in Tallinn, Estonia: Applications Open for 200 Young Changemakers
summary: The Nordic Baltic Youth Summit 2026 is inviting young changemakers from across the Nordic and Baltic region to apply for a unique youth leadership and policy-making opportunity in Tallinn, Estonia . The summit will bring together 200 young people to exchange ideas, engage in meaningful discussions, explore major challenges affecting young people and society, and develop policy recommendations for national decision-makers . Participants will have the opportunity to connect with other young leaders, challenge their perspectives and contribute their ideas to discussions on artificial intelligence, security, mental health, democracy and radicalisation. Nordic Baltic Youth Summit 2026 Overview Event: Nordic Baltic Youth Summit 2026 Location: Tallinn, Estonia Participants: 200 young people Age requirement: 18–30 years Working language: English Application deadline: 20 September 2026 at 23:59 EEST Organized by: Estonian National Youth Council Initiated and funded by: Nordic Council of Ministers and NORDBUK Who Can Apply? The summit is specifically open to young people who: Are 18 to 30 years old Live in one of the eligible Nordic or Baltic locations Can participate in the entire summit Can participate in English Are interested in the summit s key themes Are willing to contribute their ideas, experiences and perspectives Are interested in youth participation and shaping policies affecting their generation Eligible Countries and Territories Applicants must live in one of the following: Denmark Estonia Faroe Islands Finland Greenland Iceland Latvia Lithuania Norway Sweden Åland Applicants living outside these countries and territories are not eligible under the stated criteria. What Will Participants Discuss? The Nordic Baltic Youth Summit 2026 will focus on five major themes. 1. AI Leap Participants will explore the rapid development of artificial intelligence and its implications for young people and society. Discussions will consider issues including: Artificial intelligence and innovation Education and technology The future of work Opportunities and challenges created by AI The role young people can play in shaping technological development 2. Security and Resilience This theme will examine how societies can become more resilient and prepared in an increasingly complex world. Young participants will discuss: Societal resilience Preparedness Regional cooperation Emerging challenges Youth perspectives on security and resilience 3. Mental Health The summit will also provide a space for young people to discuss mental health and well-being. title: Rio Changemakers Call for Funds: Apply to Join the First Global Climate and Nature Investment Cohort
summary: Rio Changemakers is inviting impact funds focused on climate and nature to apply to become part of the first cohort featured on a new global marketplace designed to connect trusted investment opportunities with investors and locally led projects. The initiative aims to strengthen connections between climate and nature-focused capital and credible organizations working on solutions in emerging markets and developing economies. Funds selected for the first cohort will have the opportunity to help shape the platform while increasing their visibility among potential investors and accessing a growing pipeline of locally led projects seeking financing. Priority consideration deadline: 26 September 2026 About Rio Changemakers Rio Changemakers is an AI-enabled, science-guided marketplace being developed by the Government of Luxembourg and the Global Landscapes Forum (GLF) . The platform is being designed to address an important challenge in climate and nature finance: connecting credible, locally led initiatives with appropriate financing partners. The marketplace aims to make it easier for: Investors to discover trusted climate and nature investment opportunities. Locally led projects to connect with potential financing partners. Impact funds to increase their visibility among investors. Capital to reach organizations and communities already leading climate and nature action. The initiative places particular emphasis on locally led action across emerging markets and developing economies . What Is the Rio Changemakers Call for Funds? Rio Changemakers is looking for impact funds that invest in climate and nature solutions and are committed to supporting locally led action. Selected funds will become part of the platform s first cohort . This means selected organizations will have an early opportunity to interact with and test the marketplace while contributing feedback that can help improve the platform before it grows further. The call is therefore not simply an opportunity for funds to gain visibility. It is also an opportunity to participate in the development of a global financing platform intended to improve access to capital for locally led climate and nature initiatives. Who Should Apply? The call is specifically aimed at impact funds rather than individual applicants, NGOs applying for grants, students, researchers or individual entrepreneurs. Funds should have an investment strategy focused on climate and/or nature solutions and demonstrate a commitment to supporting locally led action. Rio Changemakers particularly welcomes funds that support: Indigenous Peoples Local communities Women-led organizations Youth-led organizations Other locally led initiatives Priority will also be given to funds investing in specific regions of the Global South and other emerging and developing markets. Priority Regions Rio Changemakers states that priority will be given to funds investing in: Africa Asia Latin America The Pacific The Caribbean Funds working across multiple regions may therefore be particularly relevant, especially where their investment strategies support locally led climate and nature solutions. What Types of Funds Are Encouraged to Apply? The initiative is looking for funds whose investment activities align with climate, nature and locally led development. Potentially relevant funds may include those investing in areas such as: Climate solutions Nature-based solutions Biodiversity Conservation Sustainable land management Sustainable agriculture Climate resilience Community-led environmental initiatives Locally led development Women s climate initiatives Youth-led climate initiatives Indigenous-led environmental initiatives Other climate and nature-related solutions The key consideration is whether the fund s investment strategy aligns with the objectives of Rio Changemakers. Why Join the First Rio Changemakers Cohort? Being selected for the first cohort can provide several potential benefits to participating funds. 1. Early Access to the Marketplace Selected funds will be among the first organizations to use the Rio Changemakers platform. They will have an opportunity to create their fund profile and experience the platform before it expands further. 2. Increased Visibility As Rio Changemakers develops its global marketplace, participating funds will have an opportunity to increase their visibility among investors looking for credible climate and nature investment opportunities. A presence on the platform could help funds communicate their: Investment strategy Areas of focus Geographic priorities Climate and nature objectives Approach to locally led investment 3. Access to a Growing Project Pipeline The platform is intended to connect funds and investors with a growing pipeline of credible, locally led climate and nature projects seeking financing . For participating funds, this could create opportunities to discover potential investment opportunities that align with their strategies. 4. Help Shape the Platform First-cohort participants will not simply use the platform. They will also be asked to test key features and provide feedback . Their feedback can help inform the development of a marketplace that better serves both: Investors and impact funds; and Locally led organizations seeking financing. 5. Contribute to a Global Public Good Rio Changemakers describes the marketplace as a public good intended to help make it easier for capital to reach local people and organizations already leading climate and nature action. By participating, funds can therefore contribute to a broader effort to improve the connection between capital and locally led climate and nature solutions. How the Application Process Works Interested impact funds are asked to complete an online questionnaire. The questionnaire is designed to help Rio Changemakers understand the applicant s: Fund structure Investment strategy Areas of focus Geographic priorities Approach to climate and nature investment Commitment to locally led action Readiness to participate in the first cohort Applicants should provide accurate and complete information. Where a question provides several options, applicants should select all applicable options unless the question specifically states otherwise . How Long Does the Application Take? The organizers estimate that the questionnaire will take approximately 15–20 minutes to complete. Applicants are encouraged to prepare the relevant information about their fund and investment strategy before beginning the questionnaire. Application Review Process Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis . This means applicants do not necessarily need to wait until the final deadline to apply. However, Rio Changemakers encourages interested funds to submit their applications by: 26 September 2026 for priority consideration . Funds interested in joining the first cohort should therefore consider submitting their applications as early as possible. What Happens If Your Fund Is Selected? Selected funds will become part of the first Rio Changemakers cohort. As a participating organization, your fund will have the opportunity to: Create a profile on the marketplace. Test important platform features. Provide feedback on the platform. Help identify ways the marketplace can better serve investors and locally led organizations. Increase visibility among potential investors. Potentially connect with a growing pipeline of locally led climate and nature projects seeking financing. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to funds that want to play an active role in shaping the future of climate and nature finance. Why Locally Led Climate and Nature Finance Matters One of the central ideas behind Rio Changemakers is the need to improve connections between financing and the people and organizations closest to climate and nature challenges. Locally led organizations often have deep knowledge of their communities and ecosystems and may be directly involved in developing and implementing solutions. The marketplace is intended to make it easier for investors to discover credible opportunities while helping locally led initiatives connect with financing partners. This approach places local actors at the center of climate and nature action rather than treating them simply as beneficiaries of externally designed projects. Geographic Focus Although the initiative has a global ambition, priority will be given to funds investing in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Pacific and the Caribbean . Funds with significant investment activity in these regions should therefore pay particular attention to this opportunity. The geographic focus also makes the call especially relevant to impact funds supporting climate and nature solutions in developing and emerging economies. Click HERE to read more and apply. Application Deadline Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis . For priority consideration , impact funds are encouraged to apply by: 26 September 2026 The questionnaire takes approximately 15–20 minutes to complete. Conclusion The Rio Changemakers Call for Funds offers climate and nature-focused impact funds an opportunity to become part of the first cohort of an emerging global marketplace connecting investors with credible, locally led projects. The initiative is particularly relevant to funds investing in Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Pacific and the Caribbean , as well as funds supporting Indigenous Peoples, local communities, women-led organizations, youth-led organizations and other locally led initiatives. Selected funds will gain an opportunity to create a profile, test the platform, provide feedback, increase their visibility among investors and potentially connect with a growing pipeline of climate and nature projects seeking financing. With applications reviewed on a rolling basis, interested impact funds are encouraged to submit their applications by 26 September 2026 for priority consideration . title: Pitch Perfect Africa 2026: CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship Opportunity for African Health Entrepreneurs
summary: Applications are now open for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 , a competitive pitching opportunity designed to support early-stage entrepreneurs developing innovative solutions to health-related challenges across Africa. Now in its second year, Pitch Perfect Africa provides selected ventures with an opportunity to present their innovations to experienced judges, strengthen their investment readiness, gain valuable pitching experience, and compete for financial support to further develop their work. The 2026 edition will select six H2i Level 2 ventures to participate in the virtual pitch competition. From these finalists, three ventures will each receive a CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship , providing financial support for the continued development of their ventures. The program is designed and implemented by the Health Innovation Hub (H2i) under the Africa Health Collaborative , in partnership with the Mastercard Foundation . What Is Pitch Perfect Africa 2026? Pitch Perfect Africa is a pitch competition created specifically to provide early-stage ventures within the H2i community with access to funding, pitching opportunities, mentorship-oriented learning, and investment-readiness development . The initiative recognizes that early-stage health ventures often need more than financial resources to grow. Entrepreneurs also need to be able to clearly communicate their problem, solution, target market, competitive advantage, milestones, and team to potential investors, customers, partners, and other stakeholders. Through the competition, participating ventures get the opportunity to practice these skills in a competitive environment while presenting their innovations to a panel of expert judges. The Africa edition of Pitch Perfect was introduced to the H2i African venture community in 2025 and is continuing in 2026. What Does Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 Offer? The competition provides selected ventures with several valuable opportunities for development. 1. Opportunity to Pitch to Expert Judges Six eligible H2i Level 2 ventures will be selected to pitch their innovations to a panel of expert judges. This provides entrepreneurs with an opportunity to communicate their venture to an experienced audience and receive exposure through a formal pitch competition. 2. CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship Three of the six ventures selected to pitch will be awarded an Innovation Fellowship worth CAD $5,000 each . The funding is intended to support the continued development of the winning ventures and their work. Applicants should note that fellowship payments may take approximately three to four months after the competition to be processed. 3. Investment-Readiness Development Pitch Perfect Africa is not simply about winning funding. The competition is also intended to help early-stage ventures become better prepared to engage with potential investors and other stakeholders. Through the pitch preparation process, entrepreneurs can strengthen their ability to explain: The problem their venture is addressing Their proposed solution Their value proposition Their target market Their competitors Their business or venture milestones Their team Their broader opportunity for growth These are important areas for entrepreneurs seeking customers, partnerships, investment, or additional funding. 4. Pitching Experience For early-stage entrepreneurs, the ability to deliver a clear and convincing pitch can be just as important as having a strong idea. Pitch Perfect Africa gives participating ventures a structured environment in which they can practice presenting their work, communicating their value, and responding to an expert audience. Who Can Apply for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026? The eligibility requirements for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 are specific. Applicants must meet the following requirements: Current H2i Level 2 Venture Applicants must be a current H2i Level 2 HENT venture that was onboarded by its lead mentor by August 31, 2026 . The organizers state that this requirement has no exceptions . H2i Level 2 ventures are described as ventures in the Discovery stage of H2i s four-level venture development model. Therefore, this is not an open competition for every health entrepreneur in Africa. Applicants must already meet the specified H2i Level 2 venture requirement. Previous Winners Are Not Eligible Ventures that have previously won Pitch Perfect Africa cannot apply again. However, past finalists who did not win are welcome to reapply . Ventures Outside the H2i Community Entrepreneurs and ventures that are not currently part of the H2i community are encouraged to join the H2i community as a client company. Joining the H2i community can provide access to: Mentorship Programs Venture development support Future opportunities However, simply being interested in the program does not mean a venture automatically qualifies for the 2026 competition. The specific H2i Level 2 eligibility requirement must be met. Who Is This Opportunity Designed For? Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 is designed for early-stage health entrepreneurs and health-focused ventures within the H2i African venture community , particularly ventures at the Level 2 Discovery stage. The opportunity is particularly relevant to entrepreneurs who: Are developing health-focused innovations Are currently recognized as eligible H2i Level 2 HENT ventures Want to strengthen their venture s pitch Want to improve investment readiness Are preparing to communicate their innovation to investors, customers, partners, experts, and judges Are interested in competing for financial support to continue developing their work APPLY HERE Geographic Eligibility The program is specifically connected to H2i s African venture community and is designed for African health innovation ventures within the H2i ecosystem. The information provided does not list a country-by-country eligibility list or restrict applications to particular African nationalities . Therefore, the source supports describing this as an Africa-focused opportunity for eligible H2i ventures , rather than claiming that every health entrepreneur from every African country can independently apply. The most important eligibility condition is the requirement to be a qualifying H2i Level 2 HENT venture onboarded by the lead mentor by August 31, 2026. The source also does not specify any restriction based on race or ethnicity. Important Dates for Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 Applicants should carefully take note of the competition timeline. Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass Friday, October 9, 2026 8:00–9:00 AM ET | 12:00–1:00 PM GMT The session will take place virtually through Zoom. Visit HERE to learn more about the Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 How to Apply Eligible ventures should complete the Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 application form . Applicants are encouraged to prepare their answers before beginning the submission process. The organizers recommend drafting and saving responses in a separate document before submitting the final application. This can help applicants: Review their answers carefully. Make sure all required information is included. Improve the clarity of their responses. Avoid losing work while completing the application. Present their venture consistently throughout the application. For questions about the competition or application process, applicants can contact the organizers through the provided H2i email address: h2i.international@utoronto.ca . Preparing for the Pitch Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 also includes learning opportunities designed to help ventures prepare for the competition. One of the key preparation sessions is the Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass . Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass The masterclass is designed to help early-stage health entrepreneurs improve how they communicate their ventures. It will be led by Professor Paul Santerre and will focus on the 10 key elements of a winning pitch . The session will cover areas including: Defining the problem Explaining the solution Communicating the venture s value proposition Understanding the market Assessing competition Presenting milestones Explaining the team Strengthening the overall venture story The goal is to help entrepreneurs communicate more effectively with different audiences, including: Customers Experts Partners Judges Investors Masterclass Details Date: Friday, October 9, 2026 Time: 8:00–9:00 AM ET | 12:00–1:00 PM GMT Format: Zoom Registration: The masterclass registration is available through the provided Luma registration page. Entrepreneurs need to be able to communicate their ideas in a way that allows an audience to quickly understand: What problem exists Why the problem matters Who is affected What the venture is offering Why the proposed solution is different Who the customers or beneficiaries are What the market opportunity looks like What progress has already been made What the venture plans to achieve next Why the team is capable of delivering the solution For an early-stage venture, developing these communication skills can be valuable beyond this particular competition. Important Consideration for Applicants Applicants should understand that the CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship is not automatically awarded to everyone selected for the pitch competition . Six H2i Level 2 ventures will be selected to pitch, but only three ventures will receive the CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowship . Additionally, the fellowship payment process may take three to four months following the competition . With six ventures selected to pitch and three ventures receiving CAD $5,000 Innovation Fellowships , the competition offers both financial and developmental value to participating entrepreneurs. However, applicants should pay close attention to the eligibility requirements. The competition is specifically for current H2i Level 2 HENT ventures onboarded by their lead mentor by August 31, 2026 , and previous Pitch Perfect Africa winners are not eligible. Eligible ventures should prepare their applications carefully and submit them before September 29, 2026, at 11:59 PM Eastern Time . Entrepreneurs can also take advantage of the Building a Winning Pitch Masterclass on October 9, 2026 , which is open to all and provides practical guidance on developing a stronger venture pitch. For early-stage health innovators already within the H2i ecosystem, Pitch Perfect Africa 2026 could provide an opportunity to turn a strong health innovation into a stronger, more clearly communicated and investment-ready venture. title: Temporary Staff Positions at NATO Headquarters in Brussels, Belgium – Apply to the NATO Temporary Staff Candidate Pool
summary: NATO is inviting qualified professionals to apply for its Temporary Staff (NATO HQ) candidate pool , offering opportunities to work at NATO Headquarters in Brussels, Belgium . The recruitment process is designed to create a pool of qualified candidates who may be considered for temporary positions that arise periodically across different functions within NATO s International Staff. Rather than recruiting applicants for one specific vacancy or assignment, NATO will use the candidate pool when temporary staffing needs emerge. The opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals with experience in areas such as administration, communications, project management, human resources, finance, information technology, cybersecurity, legal affairs, logistics, public diplomacy, political affairs, graphic design, event management, social media, research and analysis, and other specialized functions . Applicants should note that this is a temporary staffing database rather than a guaranteed employment opportunity. Candidates who are accepted into the pool may be contacted when an appropriate temporary assignment becomes available. Opportunity Overview NATO Headquarters occasionally needs professionals to fill temporary positions across its International Staff structure. The Temporary Staff (NATO HQ) recruitment process allows NATO to maintain a database of candidates who have relevant professional skills and may be available to take on temporary assignments. This means that applicants are not applying for one particular job description . Instead, they are applying to become part of a candidate pool from which NATO can identify suitable professionals when temporary staffing requirements arise. Temporary positions may become available in a wide variety of professional disciplines, depending on NATO s operational and organizational needs. Because these assignments can arise unexpectedly and may need to be filled quickly, NATO places particular emphasis on candidates who are capable of being available at short notice . Who Can Apply for the NATO Temporary Staff Positions? The most important eligibility requirement is nationality . Applicants must be nationals of a NATO member state . Therefore, being professionally qualified alone is not sufficient. Candidates must also meet NATO s nationality requirements. Applicants should also have: Relevant professional experience in at least one of NATO s listed areas. Proficiency in English or French . Preferably, a good working knowledge of both English and French. The ability to demonstrate the competencies expected by NATO. The ability to work effectively in an international environment. The ability to potentially take up temporary employment at short notice. The required security-clearance eligibility. Important nationality requirement This opportunity is not a worldwide open job opportunity . Applicants from countries that are not NATO member states are not eligible under the stated nationality requirement. For applicants who hold more than one nationality, NATO states that the required security-clearance certificate must be received from the government of the country or countries of which the candidate is a national. Security Clearance Requirement One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is NATO s security-clearance requirement. NATO explains that temporary positions can be urgent and may need to be filled quickly. As a result, candidates are expected to be able to obtain or reactivate the necessary security clearance rapidly. NATO therefore specifically encourages applications from candidates who: Currently hold a valid NATO security clearance , or Previously held a NATO security clearance and are able to have it reactivated quickly. Before a temporary staff member can actually be appointed, NATO must have received a security-clearance certificate with a minimum classification of NATO Secret from the government of the relevant country or countries. Why this matters Being accepted into the candidate pool does not necessarily mean that a person can immediately begin working for NATO. The security-clearance requirement is a condition of employment . A candidate must satisfy the applicable security requirements before an appointment can be made. This is particularly important for applicants who have never previously held NATO security clearance. NATO s announcement specifically states that it only encourages applications for temporary positions from people who already have, or previously had, such clearance. Professional Areas Covered by the NATO Temporary Staff Pool NATO is seeking professionals across a broad range of disciplines. Candidates can have experience in one or more of the following areas: 1. Administrative Support Professionals with experience providing administrative and organizational support may be considered. Relevant experience could include areas such as: Office administration Administrative coordination Document preparation Scheduling Records management Organizational support General administrative services 2. Cyber Defence and Cybersecurity NATO also identifies cyber defence and cybersecurity as areas in which temporary staff may be required. Professionals with relevant technical or cybersecurity experience may therefore be considered for suitable assignments. 3. Physical Security Experience related to physical security is another area identified by NATO. This can include professional experience supporting security operations, facilities, personnel or organizational security processes. 4. Defence Applicants with professional experience related to defence may be considered, including experience in: Defence planning Defence investment Related defence functions This area is particularly connected to NATO s broader institutional and operational responsibilities. 5. Emergency Response Temporary positions may also arise in emergency-response functions. Relevant experience can include: Fire response Medical emergency response Emergency preparedness Related emergency-support functions 6. Engineering and Architecture Professionals with engineering or architectural backgrounds may also be relevant to NATO s temporary staffing requirements. Candidates with experience in technical, infrastructure, construction, facilities or architectural functions may therefore be considered for suitable assignments. 7. Event and Conference Management NATO regularly operates in an international environment involving meetings, conferences, delegations and high-level events. Professionals with experience in: Event planning Conference management Meeting coordination Participant management Event logistics International events may be relevant to temporary assignments in this category. 8. Finance and Audit NATO also identifies finance-related functions, including: Budgeting Accounting Audit Financial administration Financial management Professionals with experience in these areas may be considered for appropriate temporary assignments. 9. Graphic Design and Printing Creative professionals may also qualify where their expertise is relevant to NATO s needs. This includes experience in: Graphic design Visual communications Printing Publication design Related creative production 10. Human Resources HR professionals are another potential group of applicants. Relevant areas include: Recruitment Staff services Organizational development Human resources administration Employee support HR coordination 11. Information and Knowledge Management NATO identifies several information and knowledge-management functions, including: Data entry Data encoding Document management Registry Archives Information organization Applicants with experience managing organizational information and records may therefore be considered. 12. Information Technology IT professionals may be considered for temporary positions involving: Software Hardware Information technology support Web programming Related technical functions This makes the opportunity relevant to professionals with both technical and IT-support backgrounds. 13. Legal Affairs Professionals with relevant legal experience may be considered for temporary assignments related to NATO s legal functions. Candidates should have professional expertise appropriate to legal or regulatory work. 14. Linguistic Services NATO may also require professionals working in linguistic services. This category may be relevant to candidates with appropriate language-related professional experience. 15. Logistics and Infrastructure NATO identifies several logistics and facilities-related areas, including: Supply chain management Warehouse management Stock management Infrastructure management Facilities management Professionals with operational and logistics backgrounds may therefore be eligible for suitable assignments. 16. Natural Sciences Candidates with experience in research and analysis within the natural sciences may also be considered. This category may be relevant to professionals whose expertise combines scientific knowledge with analytical or research capabilities. 17. Political Affairs Political and public-administration professionals are another important category. NATO specifically mentions experience involving: Drafting policy Diplomacy Public administration Political affairs Candidates with relevant governmental, diplomatic, policy or international-affairs experience may therefore be considered. 18. Procurement and Purchasing Professionals experienced in procurement and purchasing may also qualify for appropriate temporary positions. Relevant experience can include: Procurement processes Purchasing Supplier management Contract-related procurement activities Procurement administration 19. Project and Programme Management Candidates with project or programme-management experience are specifically included in NATO s list of relevant professional areas. This can make the opportunity relevant to professionals experienced in: Project coordination Programme management Project implementation Stakeholder coordination Planning Monitoring Delivery management 20. Public Diplomacy, Communications and Media NATO is also seeking professionals with experience in public diplomacy and communications-related fields. Relevant areas include: Press Media Journalism Communications Public diplomacy Content development Media relations Professionals working in communications and international public-facing roles may therefore be relevant candidates. 21. Web Design, Online Editing and Social Media Management Digital communications professionals are explicitly included in the opportunity. NATO lists: Web design Online editing Social media management as relevant areas of experience. This means that professionals with strong digital communications backgrounds may potentially be considered for appropriate temporary assignments. Keep Your NATO Application Updated NATO specifically instructs applicants to keep their information current in the Taleo recruitment system. This is particularly important for candidates applying to a temporary staffing pool because circumstances can change after the original application. Applicants should update information such as: Availability Security-clearance status Professional information Other relevant application details If circumstances change, candidates are instructed to edit their existing application rather than submit a new application . Documents to Submit Applicants should attach: An updated CV Relevant certifications Candidates should ensure that their CV clearly communicates their professional experience in one or more of the fields identified by NATO. For example, a communications professional should clearly highlight communications, media, public diplomacy, digital content, social media or related experience rather than submitting a generic CV. Likewise, an IT professional should clearly present relevant technical experience and certifications. What Does NATO Offer Temporary Staff? Temporary personnel receive a range of employment benefits under the applicable NATO civilian personnel framework. 38-Hour Working Week Temporary staff work a schedule of 38 hours per week . Paid Leave Temporary employees receive 2.5 paid days of leave per month worked . International Working Environment Employees have the opportunity to work within an international community at NATO Headquarters in Brussels. This can provide exposure to colleagues and professionals from different NATO member countries and a highly international institutional environment. Temporary Contract Duration Temporary staff may not normally be employed for more than six months for the same assignment under the NATO Civilian Personnel Regulations. However, if there is a later requirement, contracts may be extended for another period of up to six months . Applicants should therefore understand that these are temporary positions rather than permanent appointments. Salary and Taxation The vacancy does not provide one fixed monthly salary figure. Instead, the remuneration of temporary personnel will be specified in their individual employment contracts . NATO also states that temporary personnel s remuneration is not exempt from taxation . Temporary employees are responsible for fulfilling their tax obligations. The applicable tax arrangements may be affected by bilateral agreements between NATO and the host country concerned. Benefits Package Temporary staff are covered by a benefits package that includes several important components. Pension Contributions NATO provides pension contributions equivalent to 12% of the basic salary . Medical and Accident Benefits Temporary staff receive medical and accident benefits, including coverage relating to death and invalidity, through the NATO Group insurance contract. Paid Leave Employees receive 2.5 days of paid leave per month worked . Dependent Child Benefits For staff who meet NATO s eligibility rules, the benefits package may also include: Dependent child allowance Medical benefits coverage for dependent children Eligibility for these benefits is subject to NATO s applicable rules. Application Deadline The stated application deadline is: 6 September 2027 at 12:59 AM Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline through NATO s recruitment system. Because this is a candidate-pool opportunity, applicants should also ensure that their application remains updated after submission, particularly regarding availability and security-clearance information. Important Things Applicants Should Understand Before Applying There are several important points that potential applicants should carefully consider. 1. This is a candidate pool You are not applying for one specific temporary job. Your application is being submitted to a temporary staffing database. 2. Employment is not guaranteed Being included in the database does not mean that NATO will offer you a position. 3. NATO nationality is required The vacancy is intended for nationals of NATO member states. 4. title: Leading Change Fellowship 2026-27 in Canada: Build Leadership Skills for Sustainability, Environmental and Social Impact
summary: The Leading Change Fellowship 2026-27 is now accepting applications from young professionals and emerging leaders across Canada who want to strengthen their leadership skills, expand their professional networks, and develop the confidence to contribute to environmental and social change. Organized by Leading Change Canada , the fellowship is a virtual, cohort-based leadership development program designed for people aged 19 to 35 who are early in their professional journey, considering a purposeful career transition, or seeking to grow their capacity to lead sustainability, environmental, or social impact initiatives. The program combines expert-led workshops, peer learning, practical exercises, systems thinking, and collaborative project work. Rather than focusing solely on theoretical leadership concepts, the fellowship encourages participants to apply what they learn to real-world challenges and work collaboratively with other emerging leaders. Applications for the 2026-27 Leading Change Fellowship are currently open. About the Leading Change Fellowship The Leading Change Fellowship is designed around the idea that effective leadership requires more than technical knowledge or an impressive résumé. Participants are given an opportunity to develop practical leadership capabilities while learning alongside people from different sectors, regions, professional backgrounds, and lived experiences. The fellowship particularly supports individuals who want to create positive change but may not necessarily have a formal sustainability role or extensive experience in the field. Participants will explore the relationships between environmental resilience, financial wellbeing, and cooperation in business while developing skills that can be applied to sustainability initiatives, community projects, workplaces, and other areas of social impact. The program is delivered entirely online, making it possible for eligible participants living in different parts of Canada to participate without relocating. Why Join the Leading Change Fellowship? The fellowship offers a combination of leadership development, peer networking, practical learning, and collaborative action. 1. Gain Practical Leadership Skills Participants will develop practical skills for navigating complex challenges and creating meaningful change. The program focuses on developing leadership capabilities that go beyond simply adding another credential to a résumé. Fellows are encouraged to become more confident in their ability to understand challenges, work with others, and influence positive outcomes. According to feedback from previous Fellows: Knowledge and skills to design and lead sustainability initiatives increased by 39% . Participants reported greater confidence in their ability to influence positive outcomes. The program is therefore particularly relevant for people who want to become more effective leaders in sustainability, environmental work, social impact, business, or community initiatives. 2. Become Part of a National Community Fellows will join a community of peers from different regions, sectors, backgrounds, and lived experiences across Canada. This provides opportunities to: Exchange ideas with people working in different fields. Learn from different perspectives and experiences. Build relationships with other emerging leaders. Expand professional and personal networks. Collaborate on shared challenges. Develop connections that can continue beyond the fellowship. The program emphasizes learning from one another rather than relying exclusively on instructors or experts. 3. Turn Learning Into Action The Leading Change Fellowship is highly practical. Instead of limiting participants to lectures and theoretical discussions, the program incorporates exercises and a collaborative final project. Fellows will work with peers to develop an impact project that allows them to apply concepts and skills from the fellowship to a real-world challenge. This practical component can help participants strengthen their ability to: Work collaboratively. Identify and understand complex problems. Develop solutions. Apply systems thinking. Communicate ideas. Translate learning into action. Contribute to positive environmental or social outcomes. Previous Fellows reported a 36% increase in confidence to influence positive outcomes and a 38% increase in feeling hopeful about the future . 4. Develop Systems Thinking One of the distinctive aspects of the fellowship is its focus on understanding how different areas of society and the economy are interconnected. Participants will explore the connections between: Environmental resilience Financial wellbeing Cooperation in business This systems-thinking approach is intended to help Fellows understand that environmental and social challenges are rarely isolated problems. Instead, they can involve relationships between communities, businesses, financial systems, natural environments, policies, and individual wellbeing. Previous Fellows reported a 57% increase in their understanding of how these three areas are interconnected . Session Timing Sessions take place every two weeks on Tuesdays at: 7:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) 4:00 p.m. Pacific Time (PT) Each scheduled session may last up to two hours . Fellows are expected to attend the scheduled virtual sessions and participate actively in discussions and activities. Additional Project Commitment In addition to attending the scheduled workshops, participants will work with their peers on a collaborative impact project. Most participants should expect approximately 15–20 additional hours of project work throughout the fellowship. The exact amount of time may vary depending on the goals, scope, and requirements of each team s project. Who Should Apply? The Leading Change Fellowship may be particularly suitable for individuals who: Are between 19 and 35 years old . Live in Canada . Care about creating positive environmental or social change. Are early in their careers. Are considering a career transition. Want to strengthen their leadership capabilities. Are interested in sustainability and environmental issues. Want to understand how sustainability connects across different sectors and systems. Want to turn knowledge and learning into practical action. Are interested in learning with people who have different perspectives and experiences. Importantly, applicants do not need to have sustainability in their current job title . They also do not need to be sustainability experts. The fellowship welcomes applicants from different: Career stages Industries Educational backgrounds Professional experiences Lived experiences The program emphasizes authentic potential and a willingness to learn and contribute rather than requiring applicants to have a perfect résumé. Application Requirements The application process requires applicants to submit several components demonstrating their background, motivation, and communication skills. The application includes: Short written questions – Applicants will respond to questions designed to understand their interests, experiences, and motivation. One-minute video introduction – Applicants will provide a short video introduction. Résumé – Applicants must submit their résumé as part of the application. Applicants should therefore prepare their résumé and think carefully about how their experiences connect with leadership, sustainability, environmental issues, social impact, or positive change. Important Application Dates Applications for the 2026-27 fellowship opened on: 18 August 2026 The application deadline is: 7 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET Applicants who are selected will be notified on: 21 September 2026 The fellowship welcome and onboarding session will take place on: 29 September 2026 Because the application deadline is firm, eligible applicants should prepare and submit their applications before the closing time. What Makes This Fellowship Valuable? The Leading Change Fellowship is designed for people who want to develop leadership capabilities while exploring some of the major environmental, financial, and social challenges shaping the future. Its value comes from the combination of several elements: Leadership development Participants develop practical leadership skills and greater confidence in navigating complex challenges. Sustainability learning The program provides an opportunity to explore environmental resilience, climate solutions, sustainability, and nature. Financial perspective Participants examine financial wellbeing and the connections between financial systems, climate, and sustainability. Purpose-driven business The cooperation-in-business component introduces participants to approaches centered on democracy, equity, cooperation, and shared prosperity. Peer network Fellows become part of a national community of people with different professional and personal experiences. Practical experience The collaborative impact project allows participants to move from learning to practical application. Systems thinking Participants develop a broader understanding of how environmental, financial, business, and social systems interact. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants can strengthen their applications by focusing on authenticity and demonstrating a genuine interest in creating positive change. Rather than simply listing achievements, applicants should consider explaining: Why they are interested in leadership development. What environmental or social challenges they care about. How their current experience connects to positive change. What they hope to learn from the fellowship. What perspectives they could contribute to the cohort. How they might apply what they learn after completing the program. Why learning across sectors and perspectives is important to them. Because the program specifically states that it is looking for real people, not perfect résumés, applicants should not assume that they need extensive sustainability credentials to be competitive. A thoughtful application that demonstrates curiosity, motivation, openness to different perspectives, and a willingness to contribute may be more appropriate than trying to present an artificially perfect professional profile. When is the application deadline? The deadline is 7 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET . Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The Leading Change Fellowship 2026-27 offers an opportunity for young professionals and emerging leaders in Canada to develop practical leadership capabilities while exploring the connections between sustainability, environmental resilience, financial wellbeing, and purpose-driven business. The program goes beyond traditional leadership training by combining expert-led learning with peer exchange, practical exercises, systems thinking, and a collaborative impact project. Participants can gain new knowledge, strengthen their confidence, expand their networks, and apply their learning to real-world challenges. With applications closing on 7 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET , eligible individuals interested in sustainability, environmental change, social impact, leadership development, or purposeful career growth should consider preparing their applications early. Application deadline: 7 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET Click HERE for more fellowship opportunities.
